Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Not recorded.
- Clinical Goal(s): Clarify mental health diagnosis and current symptom burden; review efficacy/tolerability of paroxetine; ensure safety (risk assessment).
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue paroxetine as prescribed (unless advised otherwise by prescribing clinician).
  - Attend scheduled medical evaluation for acute illness; monitor any changes in mood/anxiety during this period.
  - Report any adverse effects from paroxetine or OTC medications.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Conduct comprehensive mental health assessment (including mood, anxiety, sleep, functioning).
  - Administer validated measures (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7) — if indicated.
  - Review paroxetine: indication, dose, adherence, benefits, side effects; adjust or consider referral to psychiatry/psychology as indicated.
  - Perform and document suicide/self-harm risk assessment and safety planning if needed.

Secondary Problem (if applicable): Functional impact from acute febrile illness
- Patient Goal(s): Improve physical health; reduce fatigue; maintain work functioning where safe.
- Clinical Goal(s): Coordinate with medical workup to address infection; support functional recovery; provide work accommodations as needed.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Follow through with in-person examination and blood tests as advised.
  - Rest and avoid work until cleared (per GP advice).
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Coordinate care with acute medical team; integrate outcomes into mental health review.
  - Consider fit note/work accommodations.
  - Reassess mental health status after acute illness stabilizes.
